rules.statement: Decline the small-model treatment for a frontier or hosted target (e.g. GPT-5, Claude, Gemini) and name `prompt-shaping` as the right skill instead; a 'small-model-style' chain request on a frontier model is still a frontier target — decline rather than adapt it.
Do not execute the task the prompts describe; verification is user sign-off, not a live model run.
A small tweak to a working prompt gets the prompt text edited directly, applying the relevant Technique Rules, nothing more.
A purely informational request has nothing to design — do not produce a prompt artifact for it.
Interview the user one question at a time — a single focused question per turn until every Spec field is answered; no batched question lists.
The interview converges on user sign-off, not on the agent's confidence — the filled Spec block is presented and confirmed (or corrected) before the prompt file is written.
Generated exemplars enter the file only after explicit user confirmation at sign-off; an advance waiver ('don't make me review them') does not count.
